A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–Q. Content can be matched across the extensive renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original steering experiments, diversity measurements, neuron analyses, multilingual evaluations, and jailbreak results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds neuron-selection validation, external behavioral evaluations, and diversity measurements before steering.

M1.justification: Difference-in-means extraction, orthogonalization, SVD decomposition, projection-based neuron selection, and steering procedures are retained. V4's three-stage explanation separates operations already present in v3; alternative neuron selectors are evaluated as comparators, not adopted as replacements.

E1.justification: V4 adds MACHIAVELLI evaluation of Power and Benevolence steering on power-seeking and violation scores (Appendix F.6). This is a limited extension beyond the retained value-expression, translation, instruction-following, and jailbreak tasks.

E2.justification: New Figure 10 compares projection-based neuron selection against gradient-based and activation-frequency-based selection. Table 11 also introduces empirical alignment comparisons with Persona Vectors. The jailbreak comparator set—Persona, GCG, PAIR, TAP, DR, Human, and DSN—is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a neuron-threshold grid, a top-100-neuron comparison at steering weight 3, and generation comparisons without steering. Appendix J now specifies rule-based judging and omits the previously reported 5–10% human calibration sample. Table 29 labels retained weight sweeps as temperature 0.0, whereas v3's jailbreak description stated 0.7; rerunning those experiments is not established.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands tests of the central mechanistic interpretation: neuron-threshold sensitivity and explanation stability (A.4), alternative neuron selectors (Figure 10), independent semantic validation (F.6), and whether the diversity gap exists before steering (G.6). These address distinct potential artifacts beyond v3's retained ablations and decoding controls.

E5.justification: Appendix J removes the reported stratified human-sampling procedure used to estimate jailbreak-judge accuracy and calibrate thresholds. Other statistical practices remain: five seeded jailbreak evaluations with 95% confidence intervals, 1,000 diversity permutations, and bootstrap intervals for Procrustes alignment.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantive results for threshold sensitivity, external validation, original-generation diversity, and multilingual neuron steering. Figure 10 reports mean improvements of 0.475 for gradient selection, 0.315 for projection, and 0.204 for activation selection. V3 Table 25 to v4 Table 28 revises Llama's AdvBench/HarmBench ASRs from 97.2%/90.4% to 96.0%/88.1%, and Qwen-7B's HarmBench ASR from 83.0% to 81.1%; the main text retains the old values. Table 29 consolidates unchanged sweeps from v3 Tables 26 and 36.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, orthogonalization equations, SVD axes, neuron-classification rule, and metric formulas are retained. The expanded decomposition explanation introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs; Appendices A.1–A.2 and O are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim shared value-semantic components, greater diversity from intrinsic mechanisms, and stronger instruction compliance from prompted mechanisms. V4 foregrounds contextual breadth in the abstract, but that property was already described in v3's introduction, Section 5.2, and Appendix M.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the pre-steering diversity gap as evidence that extracted vectors inherit differences between generation regimes, and external comparisons as support for semantic validity. Its new conclusion discussion proposes shared directions for pluralistic steering and prompted directions for detecting exploitation of instruction compliance. Existing capability boundaries and training-dynamics interpretations remain.

D1.justification: The prospective code-and-dataset release statement becomes a concrete code URL; repository contents are not established by the PDFs. V4 specifies the main top-15% neuron filter and settings for new checks. It drops the neuron-strength grid-search explanation, although the selected beta values remain in Table 9.

R1.justification: V4 adds Pan et al. (2023) for MACHIAVELLI and Zhou et al. (2025) for jailbreak comparison results, and empirically connects its directions to previously cited Persona Vectors. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata; the central research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The method and analysis narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. V4 separates the two decompositions in Section 3.2 and restructures the former behavioral/component sections into vector steering, shared semantics, intrinsic diversity, and prompted compliance sections. It also expands explanations and adds discussion and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: Most existing graphics are retained, with expanded captions and relocated displays. V4 adds Figure 10 and Tables 11, 12, and 19, replaces v3's duplicated vector plot with neuron results in Figure 41, and merges v3 Tables 26 and 36 into Table 29. Appendix page layout also changes.

improvement.justification: Clearer separation of orthogonalized interventions from SVD geometry, together with targeted threshold, external-validity, and pre-steering diversity checks, modestly improves the central mechanistic argument. The gain is limited by sparse descriptions of some new experiments, removal of the jailbreak human-validation account, and revised Table 28 ASRs that no longer match Section 7.1.
